blurb: Shaggy Tibetan monastery dog with snowshoe feet, a terrier in name only
description: The Tibetan Terrier is a medium-sized, square dog from Tibet with a long, shaggy double coat and broad snowshoe feet, described as affectionate and lively.
answer: The Tibetan Terrier is a medium-sized dog that originated in Tibet, where it is known as the Tsang Apso. Despite its English name it is not a terrier; European travellers named it for its resemblance to terrier breeds. It stands about 36 to 41 cm and has a long, shaggy coat.

body: Tibetan Terriers are said to have been bred in Tibetan monasteries for 2,000 years as good luck charms, watchdogs, herding dogs and companions. Dr. Agnes Greig brought the first one to Europe in 1922, and her first litter was born in 1924. The Kennel Club of India gave the breed its present name in 1930, and the American Kennel Club recognized it in 1973.

It is a powerful, square dog, typically about 36 to 41 cm and 8 to 14 kg, resembling a miniature Bearded Collie. Its broad, flat feet with hair between the toes act as natural snowshoes. The profuse double coat has a topcoat like human hair, and a fall of hair covers the face. All colours are allowed except liver and chocolate.

The breed is commonly described as amiable and affectionate, sensitive to its owners and gentle with older children if properly introduced. It tends to be reserved with strangers, has a deep bark and can bark excessively. Clever and determined, it can be stubborn, and some dogs guard their resources.
Sources describe it as suitable for apartment living but energetic, needing regular exercise; it often does well in agility and other dog sports. The long coat needs occasional trimming in pet dogs.

A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.8 years. Conditions reported in the breed include canine neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis, for which a DNA test exists, and primary lens luxation linked to the ADAMTS17 gene.

faq.q: Is the Tibetan Terrier a real terrier?
faq.a: No. It was named by European travellers for its resemblance to terriers but is not a member of the terrier group.
They do not shed like short-coated dogs, instead losing hair at a rate similar to humans, though puppies drop their coat at about nine months.

faq.q: How long do Tibetan Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.8 years for the breed.

faq.q: Is the Tibetan Terrier recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 209 in Group 9, Companion and Toy Dogs.
